verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim. 20.04.03:69-70 'the entitlement is format-agnostic (one purchase entitles all offered formats)'; :95 'Library, indefinitely, all offered formats'; :140 calls the library 'the entitlement's permanent, format-agnostic home'; D-08 (:161) 're-download any offered format forever'; DT-05 (:130) explicitly REJECTS format-bound entitlement naming the bought-MP3-want-FLAC case as 'a streaming-era mistake'. The library file states the opposite three times with no marker: 20.06.03:24 're-downloads in the format purchased', :34 'in the formats', :67-69 'the fan re-downloads the original purchased formats ... whatever the release offered and they bought', D-01 (:168) 'in the purchased formats'. Grep confirms 'format-agnostic' appears only in 20.04.03 and never in 20.06.03. Two normative statements, neither provisional, on the same surface: the library either offers a format selector across all offered formats or restricts to those bought.

Quotes verbatim. 20.04.03:108 'The payout plan version is bound at payment settlement, not at add-to-cart'; 20.04.04:99 'Split applied at payment authorization against the plan version live at that instant', repeated at :115, :120, :121. Authorization and capture/settlement are distinct events and both files posit mid-checkout split edits, so the divergence is real and unmarked. Downgraded from blocking: 20.04.03's own cell cites '(20.04.04)' as the authority in the same sentence, and 20.04.04 — the payout owner per 20.04 index D-02 — says authorization four times consistently, so an implementer has a clear ownership tie-break. The finding's secondary claim that 20.04.04 'mixes the two internally' at :44 does not hold: 'visible to that payee the moment the sale clears' describes accrual visibility, not version binding.

Quotes verbatim: 20.07:110 D-05 'k-anonymity floor on the map'; :69 same, 'Ties to 20.02.01 DT-03'; fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:255 CX-10 §3 'aggregate geo-density is unfloored map data'; :55 CX-01 §3 'counting/record-view is unfloored'; 20.02.01:99 DT-03 'the floor belongs on send and on export, not on counting or record viewing'. 20.07 D-05 cites DT-03 as authority while concluding the opposite for an aggregate surface. Downgraded from blocking: the underlying policy is tracked (20.02.01 DT-03 'Escalated to /create-prd-security', formalised as 20.02.01 Q-01, User, /create-prd-security), 20.07 carries file-level '[SURFACE]' status (:5), and a reconciling reading exists (a display-suppression floor on sparse cells is a different object from the send/export targeting floor). Divergence on whether the map suppresses sub-k cells nonetheless survives.

CX-14 does not assert the keep-vs-lose policy — it explicitly defers it. fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:343 'The keep-vs-lose policy is owned by 20.05 (its open Q-01: does a lapsed member keep what they downloaded?)'; :354 the synthesis block is stamped '*(Medium confidence — pending 20.05.02 Q-01 resolution)*'; :359 'the keep-vs-lose policy (whether previously downloaded copies survive) is the unresolved 20.05.02 Q-01 that must be answered before this edge is fully specifiable'. The 'fail-closed to locked' at :356/:359 is scoped to the state-transition race (a lapse landing mid-view), not to which items are retained, and :357 already draws the retained/re-locked line. The interim default is stated identically and consistently in the three feature files (20.05.02:73, 20.05.01:78, 20.06.03:114), with the final ruling tracked as 20.05.02 Q-01 ([OWNER], /create-prd, per 20.05.01:78). Documented deferral with owner and target.

The central claim — 'the policy exists nowhere' and the implementer must invent 'the window, the limit, whether deferred or suppressed, and who sets it' — is false. 20.01.03:44 'Frequency is a per-(fan, entity) setting'; :50 Highlights = 'At most 1 marketing email per calendar month from this entity ... The 2nd+ marketing send in a month is dropped, not queued | Cap is per-entity, not global'; :61-62 send-time resolution requires 'the tier's frequency cap is not already exhausted for the period'; D-05 (:163) locks the tier set and states '20.03 resolve[s] deterministically'. That is a per-fan, per-artist cap with a window, a limit, an over-limit behaviour and an owner. The finding also inverts DT-04 (20.03.03:81): DT-04 calls throttling 'a fleet-wide ceiling, artist-blind' and frequency capping 'a per-fan, per-artist budget' — exactly what 20.01.03 defines — so the argument that 20.01.03's tiers 'cannot supply it' rests on a misreading. Residual defect is a wrong pointer (20.03.03:93 names 20.02, which owns none of it) plus a stale '-cx.md frequency-fatigue thread' reference (20.03 CX has only CX-01..CX-05), not a missing policy.

Quotes verbatim but the two statements are scoped to different surfaces and converge. 20.01.02:23 grants the Musician on-demand single-fan evidence-chain lookup (and :85 frames it as a compliance artefact: 'Consent evidence requested during a spam complaint ... exports the full immutable event chain for one fan'). 20.01.03:24 bars a *feed* and an *edit surface*: 'no per-fan toggle history as an editable object ... cannot see a per-fan feed of who rejected what — only the roll-up'; D-04's rationale at :162 is likewise 'Per-fan unsubscribe feeds train artists to take it personally'. Every reasonable reading converges on: consent-owner surface = on-demand per-fan evidence chain, read-only; preference-centre surface = aggregate roll-up, no write path, no stream. The finding itself concedes the carve-outs bear this reading.

The governing rule is settled and the file points at it. 20.01.04:57 carries a documented-form marker '[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening] on whether stale consent (Q-02 on 20.01.02) blocks' — and 20.01.02 Q-02 (:154) reads 'Default is fixed (consent never auto-expires; staleness ≥24 months is surfaced and deliverability-downgraded but blocks no send, per the edge-case table)', with the behaviour spelled out at 20.01.02:84 and the import outcome at :88 ('records land in the artist-asserted (unmarketable-until-re-permissioned) tier'), reinforced by 20.01.04 D-03. The 'stage already run' premise also fails: 20.01.04 is '[PARTIAL]' (:5) and the 20.01 index is '[BREADTH]' (:5), so further deepening is live work, not a closed stage. What remains missing is one User-Sees copy string, which is downstream surface detail over a settled rule.

All four markers exist verbatim (20.01-cx.md:41, :42, :64, :104) and all four use the documented '[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]' form carrying a target stage; the CX file's own sub-domain status is '[BREADTH]' (20.01 index:5), which flags the file as not-yet-deep. Three are additionally answered or properly routed, as the finding concedes: :41 by 20.01.02:88 and 20.01.04 D-03; :64 by 20.01.01:25 'a merge is silent to the fan (CX-02)'; :42 by 20.01.04 Q-01 (User, /create-prd-security); :104 by 20.01.05 Q-02 (User, /create-prd). The finding's own forcedInvention field states 'Nothing product-level for three of them'. Stale-but-well-formed markers on a [BREADTH] synthesis file force no product invention.

The quote is verbatim — 20.02.01:44 lists source domain '20.04' for the Membership family — and the pointer is indeed wrong: membership state is owned by 20.05.01 per 20.02.02:34, fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:183 CX-07 §1 ('Membership state is owned by 20.05.01 ... the score reads it') and the 20.05 index. But nothing product-level diverges: the dimension itself ('tier / joined-since date / active vs lapsed') is identical under either reading, and the correct owner is stated unambiguously in a sibling file, the domain CX and the 20.05 index. Two competent implementers build the same Membership segment dimension; only a citation is stale.

Verified verbatim: 20.02.02:72 and :73 both end in a bare '`[PENDING]`' in the User Sees column with neither owner nor deferral stage — malformed tracking, not the documented mechanism. The same file demonstrates the well-formed convention one row later at :78 ('`[PENDING — /create-prd-architecture]`'), so this is a formedness defect, not house style. Held at warning rather than blocking because the underlying policy is in fact settled in the same file's decision table — D-04 (:117) 'Withhold the score rather than show a low-confidence one' and D-01 (:114) 'Attendance (scans) outweighs spend' — so what the markers block is edge-case surface copy, and they wrongly signal that decided policy is still open.

Both quotes are verbatim but they describe one gate, not two outcomes. What D-03 (20.02.03:96) blocks is the over-promise — granting an entitlement that cannot be honoured — and the edge case at :54 states the same gate's two exits: 'Narrow the audience, or say plainly that it's first-come.' Declaring first-come removes the over-promise rather than proceeding with one, which is exactly DT-02's (:76) reasoning that the harm is 'an invitation to a disappointment' and the check 'must be blunt rather than a warning nobody reads'. Blunt describes a forced choice at grant time; the User-Sees copy enumerates both branches of that choice. Competent implementers converge on a blocking interstitial with two exits.

The resolution is in the same file, dated later, and explicitly resolves the same hypothesis. 20.03.02 DT-02 (:85) is written as conditional — 'REJECTED **as currently scoped**' — and ends 'Escalated to `/ideate-validate`'; Q-04 (:119) is that escalation returning: 'RESOLVED — yes, and the decision was taken. meta/constraints.md § Project Surfaces now declares Mobile (PWA) in v1 ... Ratified as ideation-index D-28 ... So push is not lost: it arrives in v1 as PWA web push', dated 2026-07-18, with the iOS home-screen caveat carried forward. 20.06.02 Q-01 (:124) records the identical resolution. No implementer reaching the file's Open Questions can conclude push is out of v1. The residual defect is un-annotated stale Behavior prose at :40-44, not an unresolved product question.

Quotes verbatim (20.04.01:34 'A product declares exactly one kind'; the members-item row at :45; the prose at :52-53). But the prose sits directly beneath the table and is explicit and normative: '`members-item` is a **gate flag** on any other kind, not a seventh kind — a members-only download is a `digital-download` with `visibility = members` and an entitlement requirement (20.02.03).' That leaves no room for a competing build: the kind enum excludes it, a visibility field carries it. The 'seventh vs sixth' slip is a prose miscount with no behavioural consequence, and the price-rule table at :65 independently corroborates the gate reading ('requires the `members-item` gate or a member segment').

Verified verbatim and genuinely inconsistent. 20.04.04:58 parameter table: 'Rolling reserve | 10% of each **disbursement** held 90 days'. Against it, three per-sale/accrual statements: :99 happy path 'each accrues immediately, each with a 10% reserve held for 90 days'; :29 Role Lens 'Sees per sale where the money went: gross, platform cut, each payee's share, the 10% rolling reserve held'; :135 States 'Per-sale breakdown: ... 10% reserve held'. D-08 (:175) is silent on the timing. The difference is product-visible: whether the drummer's balance reads £1.26 or £1.13 and which figure the £20 disbursement threshold (:56) is measured against. Not covered by Q-06 (:189), which tracks only the reserve's size and window.

The standalone case is expressible and every statement of the policy is bundle-scoped. 20.04.01:43 'physical-record ... pre-order window allowed' and :66 the `presale` price rule 'charged now, fulfilled at/after release_at' make a bare vinyl pre-order (no digital component, therefore not a `bundle`) a first-class configuration; neither mentions segregation, and 20.04.02 never mentions it. Every normative statement names bundles: 20.04.03 D-03 (:156) 'Pre-order bundles carry the same fund-segregation policy as crowdfunding', 20.05 index D-03 (:60), 20.05.05:92. The hazard is named at fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:319-321 ('artists will route around it by calling every campaign a pre-order') and CX-13 §1 (:331 block) states 'One policy must govern both, or the policy is optional' — but the general principle is stated only in the CX, while the operative rules name the narrower class. Held at warning because the CX principle points a careful implementer the right way.

The quote at 20.04.01:185 is verbatim, but DQ-R2-01 is a live owner-decision record, not a dead audit-queue pointer, and it has since been ratified — with the answer now in the ideation tree itself. ideation-index.md:260 D-75: 'DQ-R2-01 a representation edge carries TWO independent flat axes ... domains, a subset of the commercial-domain set (live booking / recording / publishing / sync / merch). An action is authorised iff its verb is in the edge's activities and its domain is in the edge's domains'. Restated at 01.03.03:118 D-11 ('ratified by the owner 2026-07-29') and specified at 01.03.02:25 with the enum inline. The domain axis a delegate's edge must carry is therefore defined; the file's refusal to make the taxonomy call was correctly routed and the route delivered.

Verified. 20.05.01:50 routes physical-class benefits to '[20.05.05] fulfilment surface' and :82 imposes a hard publish gate — 'cannot be published without an address-collection + fulfilment path attached | Artist: blocked at tier publish until fulfilment is wired.' 20.05.05 carries none of it: Overview/Behavior (:32-47), happy path (:51-56), edge cases, D-01..D-05 and Q-01..Q-04 are entirely campaign-backer funds, tranches and milestones; its Cross-Cut Notes (:91-99) name only crowdfunding and pre-order bundles; its Role Lens Fan (:28) is scoped to 'own backing'. A grep of domain 20 finds 'address collection' only in these two 20.05.01 cells, and the 20.05 CX map (CX-01..CX-05) has no membership-fulfilment edge. The gate's satisfaction criteria — where and when a member's address is captured, how a recurring obligation is tracked — exist nowhere, so the gate cannot be built as specified.

The identifier collision is verified verbatim in one table: 20.06.02:127 '| Q-04 | **[OWNER]** **Per DQ-04.07 / D-06 — is the alert radius the same setting as `20.01.03`'s?** ... | User | `/create-prd` |' and :128 '| Q-04 | ✅ Resolved Step 5 → D-07 ... | Agent | Resolved |'. D-07 (:117) 'Resolves Q-04' therefore asserts closure of a row that is explicitly open, and any downstream stage keyed on '20.06.02 Q-04' cannot tell which item it holds. One evidence element in the finding is inaccurate and I discount it: D-06 at :116 does not contain 'See Q-04' (it says 'See Behavior → Resolved defaults' and records the radius conflict in prose). The primary defect stands on the two verified rows.

Arithmetically verified by parsing the Confidence column of the map at fanbase-direct-to-fan-cx.md:12-25: CX-01..CX-11 High, CX-12 Medium (:23), CX-13 High, CX-14 Medium (:25) — 12 High, 2 Medium. The header at :5 states '14 intra-domain pairs confirmed (13 High, 1 Medium), 5 rejected. All High pairs carry full 5-question synthesis.' Both Medium rows carry qualified synthesis (:301 '*(Medium confidence — synthesis provisional)*'; :354 '*(Medium confidence — pending 20.05.02 Q-01 resolution)*'), so the header's completeness attestation is counting a set it has miscounted. Warning: no product behaviour is forced, but the file's own self-attestation is unusable for judging how many edges are provisional.
